title: UI Audit Acceptance · Taskboard (example)
subtitle: Bundled example audit — open app/index.html to see the audited page

scope.request: Example: audit the Taskboard demo app's main board

references.description: All semantic colors come from :root tokens (--accent/--ok/--warn/--muted); components never hard-code hex values

unknowns: Single-page demo app; baseline inferred from its only stylesheet

coverage_plan.notes: Example audit: one screen, one environment (QUICK tier)

evidence.notes: Initial state. 'Add task' is disabled but visually identical to the enabled 'Import' button

steps: inspect stylesheet tokens and component rules
evidence.notes: Token set defines --warn but .tag.due hard-codes #c9a227; no :disabled rule exists for .btn

findings.title: Disabled primary button is indistinguishable from an enabled one
findings.summary: 'Add task' is disabled until the input has text, but it renders exactly like the enabled 'Import' button next to it — same background, border, text color, and pointer cursor.
findings.expected: Disabled controls have a perceivable visual downgrade (opacity within the existing token language) and a not-allowed cursor.
findings.actual: No :disabled rule exists in the stylesheet; both buttons share identical computed styles.
findings.user_impact: Users click a dead button with no feedback and assume the app is broken.
findings.root_cause: .btn/.btn.primary define no :disabled variant, so the disabled attribute only blocks events
findings.recommendation: Add .btn:disabled { opacity: .45; cursor: not-allowed; } using existing tokens (see DEMO-001 variant B)

findings.title: Due-date tag hard-codes a hex color instead of the --warn token
findings.summary: The .tag.due badge uses #c9a227 while the project defines --warn (#b3720a) for warning semantics; every other semantic color on the board goes through a token.
findings.expected: Semantic colors come from :root tokens per the inferred baseline.
findings.actual: .tag.due { color: #c9a227; border-color: #c9a227; } bypasses the token set.
findings.user_impact: Warning color drifts from the rest of the product and will not follow future token updates.
findings.root_cause: Hard-coded hex value predating the token set

demos.title: Disabled-button affordance: current vs dimmed proposal

b.label: Proposed (:disabled dims via opacity, existing tokens only)

demos.rationale: Uses only the existing token language; opacity plus cursor communicates the disabled state without introducing new colors.
risks: Opacity value should be re-checked against the real page background before implementation
demos.user_question: Accept dimming disabled buttons via opacity?

reviews.note: Bundled example; a real audit uses independent reviewers

continuation.note: Example audit: decisions here are for demonstration only
